conventions.arkit_channels: 3D recipes use the 52-channel ARKit blendshape vocabulary, the naming shared by Unreal Live Link Face / MetaHuman, Blender face-rig tooling, and VRM face-tracking maps. Only non-zero channels are listed; unlisted channels are 0.
conventions.fun_semantics: The canonical 'fun' is PLAYFUL (amused, teasing, enjoying herself), per Matt's 2026-10-06 decision. It is not VRM 1.0 'relaxed' (calm). On VRM 1.0 export it ships as a custom expression named 'fun'; do not alias it to the relaxed preset, which would change the sculpt's meaning.
conventions.vrm: v0 = VRM 0.x preset name, v1 = VRM 1.0 preset name. 'custom' means the emotion ships as a named custom expression in both spec versions.
conventions.weights: All weights are 0.0 (neutral) to 1.0 (full). Emotion morphs are a layer: blink, gaze, and viseme groups compose additively on top and are never baked into an emotion.

emotions.animation_notes: All channels 0. Blink and idle breathing carry the life; never sculpt expression into the base mesh.
emotions.role: Rest face and the base every other expression is a delta from. The game's Expression::Neutral; the only expression that ships today.

sprite_2d.eyes: open, relaxed lids, gaze at viewer
sprite_2d.mouth: closed, flat or the faintest natural curve

emotions.animation_notes: Scales cleanly 0.4-1.0. The 'celebrate' sheet mood is this template at full weight plus a pose; keep them the same face.
emotions.role: Warm, genuine pleasure. Default positive reaction: good work, a joke landing, a level cleared.

sprite_2d.extras: cheek shading lifts with the smile
sprite_2d.eyes: soft upward curve (happy squint), lower lids raised
sprite_2d.mouth: open or closed smile, corners clearly up, slight cheek raise

emotions.animation_notes: Reads at 0.6+; below that it blurs into determined. Differentiate by nose sneer and brow depth.
emotions.role: Real anger: confronted, cheated, protective. Stronger than annoyed; use sparingly so it keeps its weight.

sprite_2d.brows: drawn down and together, inner ends lowest
sprite_2d.eyes: narrowed, upper lids pressed down, hard stare
sprite_2d.mouth: pressed flat or open shout shape; frown corners

emotions.animation_notes: browInnerUp does most of the work; if the sculpt can only keep one channel, keep that one.
emotions.role: Sorrow and disappointment: loss, failure she takes personally, sympathy.

sprite_2d.brows: inner ends raised and drawn together (the grief angle)
sprite_2d.extras: tear variants are separate overlays, not part of this template
sprite_2d.eyes: upper lids lowered, gaze slightly down, lower lid tense
sprite_2d.mouth: small frown, corners down, lips closed

emotions.animation_notes: Animate fast in (100-150 ms), hold briefly, decay into the follow-up emotion. A held surprise reads as a mask.
emotions.role: Startle and astonishment: outages, jump scares, sudden news. Short-lived by nature.

sprite_2d.extras: pairs with the 'alarmed' sheet mood; alarmed adds worried's brow tension
sprite_2d.eyes: wide open, full iris visible, small pupils

emotions.animation_notes: Asymmetry is the signature: symmetric fun collapses into happy. Keep the left-smile bias consistent across characters unless a character sheet says otherwise.
emotions.role: Playful and teasing: she's enjoying this, mischief included. Games, banter, winning. NOT calm/relaxed.

sprite_2d.brows: one brow quirked up, the other level
sprite_2d.extras: head tilt is a pose, not part of the face template
sprite_2d.eyes: bright, slight happy squint, maybe a half-wink energy without closing
sprite_2d.mouth: asymmetric grin, one corner higher, teeth optional

emotions.animation_notes: Partial eyeBlink weights give the half-lidded look; keep blink-group animation from fully closing over it (blink layer clamps at 0.8 when annoyed > 0.5 is an art call, tune per character).
emotions.role: Irritation and deadpan: the flat stare, the sigh before the sentence. The 'pout' sheet mood is this family with a pushed lower lip.

sprite_2d.eyes: half-lidded, unimused stare, gaze level or slightly aside
sprite_2d.mouth: flat line or small tight frown; pout variant pushes the lower lip

emotions.animation_notes: Sad is worried with the eyeWide removed and frown deepened; keep the two sculpts distinct in the brow tension.
emotions.role: Anxiety and concern: something might go wrong, someone might be hurt. Softer than sad, tenser than neutral.

sprite_2d.brows: inner ends raised like sad but shallower, with tension
sprite_2d.extras: sweat drop is a separate overlay convention, not part of the template
sprite_2d.eyes: slightly wide, gaze toward the problem
sprite_2d.mouth: small, stretched, uncertain; corners neither up nor down

emotions.animation_notes: The morph alone under-reads without the blush layer; rigs must pair this key with the blush texture toggle. Gaze aversion sells it in motion.
emotions.role: Flustered and caught out: compliments, mistakes, the blush family. The 'blush' sheet mood is this template's cheek component.

sprite_2d.extras: blush marks across cheeks/nose are REQUIRED for the read; in 2D they are drawn, in 3D they are a texture/shader layer, not a morph
sprite_2d.eyes: gaze down and aside, lids soft
sprite_2d.mouth: small nervous closed smile or wobbly line

emotions.animation_notes: Angry is determined plus noseSneer and deeper brow; if a determined sculpt reads angry, cut browDown to 0.4 before touching anything else.
emotions.role: Resolve and focus: the work face, the boss-fight face. Positive tension, jaw set, no sneer.

sprite_2d.brows: lowered levelly, straight, no inner pinch
sprite_2d.eyes: direct stare, lids firm, no squint-narrowing

emotions.animation_notes: Like fun, asymmetry is the signature; smug is fun with the warmth removed (less cheek, more lid).
emotions.role: Self-satisfied and superior: she knew it all along. Bianca's home turf; use as seasoning, not a default.

sprite_2d.extras: chin lift is a pose, not part of the face template
sprite_2d.eyes: half-lidded, looking slightly down at the viewer

procedural_groups.note: Not emotions. These compose over any emotion and are defined once for every character, following the VRM 1.0 grouping.

purpose: Canonical emotion templates for Light Show companions across sprites, portraits, and animatable 3D models. One canonical key per emotion drives: 2D sprite-sheet face rows, dialogue portrait expressions (game/src/waifu/dialogue_ui.rs Expression enum: Neutral + these 10 = the planned 11-expression sheets), and 3D morph targets / blendshapes in Blender, Unreal, Godot, Redot, and Unity.

sheet_mood_mapping.alarmed: surprised with worried brow tension (browInnerUp added)
sheet_mood_mapping.blush: embarrassed (cheek component; pair with neutral or happy at low weight)
sheet_mood_mapping.celebrate: happy at full weight, plus pose
sheet_mood_mapping.note: The existing 2D companion sheet moods (light-show game/src/waifu/sprite.rs MOOD_ROWS) in terms of the canonical templates, so sprite, portrait, and 3D work stay the same faces.
sheet_mood_mapping.pout: annoyed with pushed lower lip (mouthShrugLower emphasis)
sheet_mood_mapping.wink: procedural blinkRight held, over happy or fun

weights_status: ARKit recipes are v1 starting weights for sculpting and tuning, ratified as templates on 2026-10-06. They are expected to be tuned per character against renders; the canonical keys, VRM mapping, and fun semantics are the stable contract, the numbers are the adjustable part.
